$comment: COMPLY.2 (task-366): the path to rule-list table. DATA, not code, decides which rule lists govern a task: scripts/analysis/backlog-lane.mjs resolves a task's `Files:` line through it at launch, scripts/hooks/check-lane-close.mjs resolves it again at close. Operator, verbatim, 2026-11-20: "Add the tasks to incr 1b - the infa freeze needs to be lifted again - what is the point of building a mess - wasted effort." (record ~/Buildo-scratch/queues-20261113/MORNING-DECISIONS.md, the 2026-11-20 entries).

A list is used WHOLE: `whole` = the file, `sections` = whole sections picked by heading (a heading text is matched at its start, after leading emoji and punctuation; the section runs to the next heading of the same or a higher level); a section is allowed only where the file itself separates rules from history or narrative. Never a hand-picked clause.

A row maps path globs to lists. `globs` are literal; `globs_from` REUSES an existing path map (mcbylaws/protected-paths.json keys layer23 = by-law code and frontend = McFrontend surface paths; Spec 133 R-KP / R-LD, Spec 128 section 4.11) instead of copying it; `imports_from` makes the row fire only for a file that imports from that path. Several rows may match: the lists are the union.

`exempt` globs are records the lane writes itself (the commit hooks always allow them, check-task-files.mjs): they resolve to NO list and the brief says so. A Files entry no row and no exempt glob matches is refused at launch with the path named. `no_files_default`: a task of that type with no Files line gets the named row (record-only tasks get the queue lists). `increment_docs`: every task also gets the requirements document of its milestone group letter.

V2.LIST (task-406, McFix V2 step 1; operator 2026-11-20, see the task text): `every_task` lists are attached to EVERY task whatever its Files line (the five words in the step handbook Glossary, and the plan protocol as a repo document); `milestone_docs` attaches to a task the objectives sections of its own milestone, beside `increment_docs`; `kinds` are the examples the generated page docs/reports/generated/rule-lists-by-kind.md prints (what each kind of work receives). `rule-lists.mjs validate` refuses a table with none of them.

My recommendation: yes."): the `exempt` key (bare globs; no new field) also lists the golden snapshot files that one existing check validates, and each such glob names that check in the line below it (a test fails a golden glob with no named check). This exempts the REVIEW MATERIAL only (the close check and the launch brief take the task range minus matchesAny(exempt)); list resolution is unchanged (a golden path still matches its rows). A code file, a script, the manifest states.json or a nested file is not matched. The landing sample web_landing.sample.json is not tracked, so no glob is added for it.
